**Overview**  
**Let’s define those involved in this project and bound by this contract**

This is an Authorization to Proceed (ATP) for services to be provided by MyCompany, LLC [www.mycompany.com/](http://www.unitinteractive.com/) (AGENCY) to ClientCompany [www.website.com/](http://www.website.com/) (CLIENT).

AGENCY will be providing consulting, design, and development services to support CLIENT’s efforts for their *Website Name* website ([http://website.com/](http://website.com/)). This document is the ATP for the project to complete the objectives for which CLIENT contacted AGENCY. This document will describe the scope of work, process, deliverables, and the associated price for the project.

\- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \-

**Scope of Work**  
**Here’s what we’ll be doing together…**

**Logo Design**  
AGENCY will redesign the logo for *Brand Name*. The logo will be produced for print and web use, in color and B/W formats (if applicable). *Note that this portion of the project presupposes that this is to be just a simple, extensible logo – not an identity system* (a project requiring considerably more time and resources).

**Website Design Strategy Concept**  
The image communicated and the user experience created by your website will directly reflect on your company and suggest a corresponding level of quality to users. The objectives for the new design concept will be:

* to craft an intelligent and effective information and content architecture for the website—along with the relevant global and contextual navigation scheme(s),  
* to design an intuitive user experience based on this architecture and design,  
* and to design a brand-consistent, compelling look and feel for the website

AGENCY will work with CLIENT to create an effective design concept that highlights the reputation of CLIENT’s company and communicates effectively to the target audience(s), while facilitating the desired and useful user interaction. 

**Layout Development**  
The purpose of this objective is converting the design concept into Web pages. Base on the approved design strategy, AGENCY will create HTML and CSS page templates for the main and basic interior pages. CLIENT will then use their own resources to build the website-proper in their own content management system and make functional any forms or other mechanisms requiring back-end programming or scripting. *AGENCY will provide 1 main page template and up to 6 interior page layout templates.*

*The delivered HTML page templates will allow for a screen-size- and device-specific experience. This means that the pages and their content will adapt to display contextually to various screen sizes and devices, allowing for a highly usable experience no matter how users access the website; from desktop, table, or handheld mobile device.*

**Timeline:**   
An estimated timeline for the project involves roughly 12 weeks of work. AGENCY will provide a more specific timeline once discovery is complete and everyone’s schedules can be incorporated. The project will be managed online at AGENCY’s Basecamp site.

\- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \- \-

**Process Description**  
**…and this is how we’ll do it**

The project will commence with a discovery process, beginning with CLIENT and AGENCY meeting in person *or* by phone (**this would likely be a 2- to 3-hour call**). AGENCY will also conduct its own discovery relevant to the project, and follow-up contact by phone or email may continue the discovery process during the project. **Therefore, in-contact time on the part of CLIENT is important during the life of the project**. The result of the initial discovery will be a *Strategy Brief*, which will simply and concisely detail the project’s creative and communicative objectives as understood by AGENCY. This document will be reviewed, revised if necessary, signed/approved by CLIENT, and then the design portion of the project can begin.

**Logo:**  
On a mutually agreed upon date, AGENCY will present a small number of logo design candidates (1 to 3\) for review with CLIENT, either in-person or by phone (*phone call with internet viewing access*). The presented designs will represent differing design directions/ideas, but each will be consistent with the overall objectives of the project as outlined in the strategy brief. 

At the logo candidate review meeting, AGENCY will explain the strategies involved in the presented candidate designs and CLIENT should be prepared to offer some initial feedback as to how closely the suggested candidates meet with their needs and expectations. Within a short internal review time (1-3 days), CLIENT should select the approach that best suits their needs and discuss any points of objectives compatibility or revision with AGENCY. The design may be subjected to a limited number of revisions (up to X hours) in order to achieve the final logo design. CLIENT will then signoff on the final design. *At this point, website design can begin*.

**Website:**  
On a mutually agreed upon date, AGENCY will present one or two (AT AGENCY DISCRETION) visual and/or UX design strategies—using mockup(s) or functional prototypes—for review with CLIENT, either in-person or by phone (*phone call with internet viewing access*). If two design strategies are presented, each will represent different design directions/ideas, but each will be consistent with the overall objectives of the project as outlined in the strategy brief. Each design strategy will consist of 1 to 3 example page design/layout(s).

At the design strategy review meeting, AGENCY will explain the strategies involved in the presented designs and CLIENT should be prepared to offer some initial feedback as to how closely the suggested designs meet with their general needs and expectations. Within a short internal review time (1-3 days), CLIENT should select the design strategy that best suits their needs and assemble and deliver a list of any desired discussion points for revision (if necessary) to AGENCY. After proper discussion, the design may be subjected to a limited number of revisions (up to X hours) in order to achieve the final design strategy. CLIENT will then approve/signoff on the final design strategy.

With design approval the further necessary content, template, and modal window layouts will be crafted. With informal approval of these layouts the project enters the website production phase.

At this point the design strategy is then produced as the final cross-browser compliant, adaptive HTML/CSS pages. The Web browsers our production accounts for are the most recent 2 versions of: Firefox, Safari, and Chrome, and Internet Explorer.

**On Feedback:**   
When discussing presented designs, we want your candid feedback\! Please note, however, that your negative design feedback should come in the form of problems rather than solutions. For instance, feedback that describes how to change something or how to design some element of the user interface prevents us from bringing our own expertise to bear on the issue. It’s also a breach of contract. Good feedback describes the problem; for instance, how a specific or general business or project requirement is not adequately or properly addressed by the current strategy or by a specific feature of the design. In short, we’ll need you to point out problems you perceive rather than communicate solutions to us. You hired us as problem-solving experts. Give us the chance to exercise the expertise you’ve paid for. In fact, by signing this ATP, you are promising to do so.

**Deliverables**  
**This is what we’ll be making and delivering to you at the end of the project**

In exchange for payment of the price outlined below, AGENCY will create and deliver the following items:

* 1 logo (for Web and print purposes, in color and monochrome formats)  
* 1 main page template (html/css)  
* Up to 8 interior page layout templates (html/css)

***Note:** Web page layout comps (.psd or .png files) are not deliverables, but merely tools that your designer(s) will use to conceptualize the actual deliverables. The layout comps are just that: comps, used to approximate but not capture full detail.*

**Payment Structure**  
**This is the schedule you’ll follow for payment of invoices**

* 50% of the total project fee will be due before or at the initial Discovery Meeting ($39,879.60)  
* 25% of the total project fee will be due 6 weeks after the initial discovery meeting—*or*—upon notification for readiness for presentation of the website design concept *(whichever comes first)* ($19,939.50)  
* 25% of the total project fee will be due 12 weeks after the initial discovery meeting—or—upon notification of completion of the project *(whichever comes first)* and before delivery of the files ($19,939.50)

All project fees are due and payable upon receipt of invoice, including those for any stock photography or other purchased materials authorized for the project. Final payment is required before any files will be released to CLIENT.

***A Note on Deadlines:***  
MyCompany loves deadlines and we hit every single one of them every time. In order for us to do this for you, however, it is important that *you* hit every deadline, too. We will rely on you to keep the project flow going with your approvals and sign-offs, as well as getting us content for your website in a timely manner—typically before any design can begin. Out-of-contact time and delays in approvals will directly affect the project schedule, necessitating our moving deadlines and milestones back accordingly, *but note that payment milestones will remain as scheduled*. By signing this document, you acknowledge your responsibilities in keeping the project on-schedule. By the same token, in the unlikely event we miss one of our deadlines, the payment milestones *will* be adjusted accordingly.

It is important to note that AGENCY will run the project. **The primary designer on this project will define the process and set all deadlines—for our team and for yours.**

**And lastly, this…**  
**We can’t please everyone. In fact, we’re not even going to try.**

Pleasing everyone with our work is impossible. It wastes the time of our best customers, and annoys our staff. Great success can happen when we maintain focus upon those who are the rightful targets of the work and the message in order to bring clarity and delight. We will work with you to determine the rightful targets of our work…and it is likely that you (CLIENT) *are **not** the rightful target*. By signing this contract you volunteer your commitment to this vital standard and the trust in our expertise that it requires. If in the course of our work with you we are required to please the wrong people, our work with you must cease.

**Authorization to Proceed**  
**If all of this looks good to you, let’s formalize this agreement**

*Your commitment to this project will be directly reflected in the results. By hiring our agency you’ve enlisted our expertise at how best to accomplish the goals that your team and our team have defined. In order to accomplish those goals we require your participation and cooperation – even if you don’t fully understand some of the elements of that participation* (which we’ll work hard to make clear)*. In the end, we can only accomplish what we are allowed to accomplish; the quality of the result will depend significantly on the quality of your participation.*

AGENCY and CLIENT agree upon the responsibilities and estimates described in this Authorization to Proceed document. CLIENT agrees to pay the full fees detailed herein and authorizes AGENCY to proceed with the work described in this document based on the time estimates provided.
